newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA NEEDS TO UPGRADE ITS AIRPORTS -IATA.
newsitem.headline: INDIA NEEDS TO UPGRADE ITS AIRPORTS -IATA.

text.p: India needs to overhaul its airports and air safety systems to tap the full potential of the airline business, the International Air Transport Associaton (IATA) said on Tuesday.

"India needs to move fast towards newer air traffic control systems, cheaper jet fuel and more dynamic airports, if it has to take its place in world aviation and reap its economic benefits," IATA's director general Pierre Jeanniot told a news conference.

He said if India does not expand capacity and come up to world standards, it will not achieve prosperity that comes with an increase in air travel. "This sector has the potential to create thousands of jobs, once it is opened up."

Jeanniot said growth in air travel was straining air traffic control (ATC) resources in India. He said rapid action was taken to draw up an ATC modernisation plan, after the November mid-air collison of a Saudi plane with a Kazakh airliner near Delhi, but its implementation was behind schedule.
IATA was urging the government to implement the plan as soon as possible, particularly for the Delhi-Bombay sector, he said. There are over 20 flights a day between Delhi and Bombay.
On the price of jet fuel, he said international carriers had to pay higher rates in India. "It is a world product, and India should charge world prices."
He said the cost of jet fuel in India was 30 percent of an airlines operating cost, while in the rest of the world it was 15 percent.
He said there was no airport in India that matched London's Heathrow or Paris' Charles De Gaulle.
"Airports need to be run as business enterprises and not as government departments. The potential of the space is realised by commercialisation, and a reduction of cost to the consumer."
Jeannoit said air travellers suffer from poor airports, long delays in customs and immigration clearance and, a history of poor air safety.
"India has a huge tourism potential that can be exploited with proper air travel infrastructure," he said.
-- Sanjit Singh, New Delhi Newsroom (91) 11-301-2024; Fax (91)
